---
title: "About Minaxia"
---

Minaxia® is an openly licensed **semi-quantitative cybersecurity risk estimation method for connected and embedded products**, published and maintained by [Cylenk](https://www.cylenk.com/).

The goal is to make a practical, transparent method widely available: one that teams can inspect, apply, discuss and improve. It is available free of charge, including for commercial use under its [licence](#licence-and-attribution). You do not need to engage Cylenk to use it.

Minaxia estimates risk for already identified scenarios; it is not a complete risk assessment process. The [method](index.qmd) is the assessor-facing reference. Version {{< var method.version >}} is an initial-development release and makes no empirical-validation claim; the separate [calibration document](calibration.qmd) explains its current basis and release policy.

## Authorship and stewardship {#authorship-and-stewardship}

**Eric Seuret is the original author of Minaxia.** His background spans embedded systems, connected products and regulatory work in medical and industrial settings. He also lectures in industrial and mobile robotics at Fachhochschule Graubünden. [More about Eric](https://www.cylenk.com/en/about/).

**Cylenk SA publishes and maintains the official method**, reviews contributions and retains final editorial authority over official releases. Cylenk's focus is cybersecurity grounded in the product: its firmware, hardware, connectivity and operating constraints.

Minaxia is open to contributions beyond its original author. Contributors retain copyright in their contributions and license them under CC BY 4.0. Under that licence, Cylenk may edit and include accepted contributions in official releases published under its Minaxia trade mark, with the required attribution. Contributing does not grant any rights to the Minaxia trade mark.

## Collaboration and contributors {#collaboration-and-contributors}

Practical experience, critical review and different perspectives can help improve the method. Contributions are welcome through the [public GitHub repository](https://github.com/cylenk-labs/minaxia):

- report unclear wording or inconsistent scoring guidance;
- propose improvements with a rationale and relevant examples;
- share non-confidential application experience or suggest translations.

Use [issues](https://github.com/cylenk-labs/minaxia/issues) to start a discussion or submit a pull request for a specific change. Please read the short [contribution guidance](https://github.com/cylenk-labs/minaxia/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) first.

Substantive contributions will be acknowledged here using contributors' preferred public names, including reviews, examples and translations as well as document edits. The repository records individual changes and their authors.

## Help with a cybersecurity challenge {#cybersecurity-help}

Cylenk provides cybersecurity expertise for connected and embedded products, grounded in hands-on firmware, embedded Linux, hardware/software architecture and regulatory experience.

If you need support with a product cybersecurity challenge, [get in touch with Cylenk](https://www.cylenk.com/en/contact/).
